My story isn’t political. It’s personal. | | | [](http://links.gopwins.info/u/click?_t=98057da4e99f4c609080f212fe1184e1&_m=468280d0ef644f939c2abf71077b151b&_e=3fQ_53PYFuhXSHR9QWsDfNAboTkven_rUECo7u_eRuBEEW8OGbfMYtx-tbVazy9i0hqof6tgC_jVxMBnj3LY-0CYItLU9VUSyyYvoOE_xVBls6s2YRql1y5iMjSiUFDeKN_q1vQsGIu-qyRGzcddGAm_j5ND6ChumZZ5d5-gepmjH6PaaNIekoZyHXkJCYkrDcu6zU_e2IqW8qMjBqHbbJ71my2mVmqUoQgvbfkxJsmySR8CbUPpfVnmOF_XgJotyRlGBVTniEqWuJryJ-XBoJMxxzPUtuQnbAQtUkUth9LCusqYq-iKVYKv9Fh838zOUdnELIVzaTgpNNUsb1w5cK62UiwVJYUvXuDgcaw1LWc2XMdrHQJ1KTjV88dbYrwb-UZgVlvMOvc0DlJPeMvg3cO2T6qdg5qjqSLN1_O2Ea4%3D)

Friend, I was born in Communist China under the leadership of Chairman Mao. From the moment I could speak, I was told he was God. I saw families torn apart, neighbors reporting on neighbors, and millions of people brainwashed into silence. **My parents and I lived in constant fear.** There was no freedom of speech, no right to worship, no chance to build a better life. We had nothing — not even hope. But even as a young woman, I knew deep down that human beings are meant to be free. And so, I left. When I arrived in America in the 1980s, I only had $100 in my pocket. But this country gave me something priceless: **opportunity.** I worked hard, built a life, raised my family, became a business owner, and became a proud US citizen. America let me rediscover God, and it gave me the liberty to live by my own values, not the dictates of a dictator. [That’s why I am running for Congress as a proud conservative.](http://links.gopwins.info/u/click?_t=98057da4e99f4c609080f212fe1184e1&_m=468280d0ef644f939c2abf71077b151b&_e=3fQ_53PYFuhXSHR9QWsDfNAboTkven_rUECo7u_eRuBEEW8OGbfMYtx-tbVazy9i0hqof6tgC_jVxMBnj3LY-0CYItLU9VUSyyYvoOE_xVBls6s2YRql1y5iMjSiUFDetIILrSxy6HtKlxJiEELmAJahNc6mqeFG0dlGmOpSOLCskIHTujbav0XxTsJkp0meO3qigLkB-EiEm4i4QqJel3dXJnrIWWjmw8RkYV8N_HCSmbD7zfx8Db-UoGhNbnzBD1Fz1lGEUOGP9HOTev_sg0Q6JNOouWuayDXCKlUU4vSHVHNnI12pNlHI8URT_oPEnWTdqL0yf6_Y5zv6Hc4FmutCdR2Kz3gakEr1880lIh90LsYf33Lbxo7rJ35BPvBsTSH_mqARngnZrGo-gD3Aya75L6X2D8n5q4dQhagv-Xs%3D) I see warning signs from the Left that remind me too much of where I came from. **Government overreach. Attacks on faith and family. A culture of dependency instead of opportunity.** I refuse to sit back and let our country drift toward the same failed system I escaped. But I can’t fight this battle alone. My woke opponent, Maggie Goodlander, has the backing of Washington insiders and coastal elites. They will pour millions into this district to silence my message of freedom. That’s why I’m asking you: [will you stand with me today?](http://links.gopwins.info/u/click?_t=98057da4e99f4c609080f212fe1184e1&_m=468280d0ef644f939c2abf71077b151b&_e=3fQ_53PYFuhXSHR9QWsDfNAboTkven_rUECo7u_eRuBEEW8OGbfMYtx-tbVazy9i0hqof6tgC_jVxMBnj3LY-0CYItLU9VUSyyYvoOE_xVBls6s2YRql1y5iMjSiUFDeRcMIUx5Bd57aDPwLvdOsjxYKx03YYAVmpoJomVE9LCRqbvbshwSqUaIDp8ztSXW-O4khdnsmT5abAeyknTio2vYXziqtgM9wxs8O8tKjAAK7RObdCu878iih3PXkk-Z8jEIsnX3chDi7nyjKZukVGVJG5xNvpNtC62RISIbcs7cAS_u0xVlZ1DvcKJ8ISNsHuEdetr4jBRKDbH-mErNV3D4Z6coI3nLBfzEKgqRZLnNvYHxdlzv75TtwQIAR6WKg95ez1NyBs4KFs4rDNVPjFu_NGApfWFhCeQuC6EcRMHM%3D) [Your gift — whether $25, $50, or $100 — will help us build a grassroots army strong enough to take on the establishment.](http://links.gopwins.info/u/click?_t=98057da4e99f4c609080f212fe1184e1&_m=468280d0ef644f939c2abf71077b151b&_e=3fQ_53PYFuhXSHR9QWsDfNAboTkven_rUECo7u_eRuBEEW8OGbfMYtx-tbVazy9i0hqof6tgC_jVxMBnj3LY-0CYItLU9VUSyyYvoOE_xVBls6s2YRql1y5iMjSiUFDeWircpoXVSGwQot069qIQTXYy_aJOqGv9qPfHUU0Z5pqVFMuJzMQsUKgAe7VU7RLJNe4luXtFJQymg9tsozLN79K2ncV5Mpqm1IiSqp-m3DsKBKgPDf4gMJFh5UO8QsCoxgcLGDpfGG-xu5SHpnWfkHQItYU1hr-tsPZ679YVkMNa348k5tDwDnhDTqrW55b1E8BYco9wJy8wRzl4035WxIjjQVXzY-L1XeucG0JaVALI6d26rGO9hi8qWJ2WIAqdb9vS4nbCLhOgybV-M0f2X4Spj9l73nTE_s-ID_fzKc4%3D) It will help us get my story and our message out to every voter in NH-02.

name: Voter Action Project Research Team
subject: Private financial support for our elections?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NPR: Private funding saved the 2020 election. Now, some GOP-led states are banning it [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/NPR_PrivateFunding.png]
Private sector companies and nonprofit charities often donate money and provide grants to communities across the country to help administer voting.
This includes mail sorting machines in Philadelphia, nonpartisan voter registration staff in Arizona, and cameras to verify no one tampers with ballots in Bucks County, PA. Local officials have referred to this money as a "lifeline".
Now, 14 states have banned outside funding and five other states passed a ban that was vetoed by the Governor.
We want to hear from our supporters about your feelings about this news. Will you take our quick one-question poll right away?

**_I miss him. _**

Every breath. Every heartbeat. Every memory I now replay in my mind... I miss him.

My husband, Charlie Kirk, was the love of my life.

You may know him as a fighter for freedom. A warrior for truth. The founder of Turning Point USA. The host of a nationally syndicated radio show. A bold conservative voice that gave courage to a generation.

But to me... _He was just Charlie._

He was my best friend. The father of our two precious babies. The man who made me laugh when the world felt too heavy.

The man who, every single morning without fail, would look at me and ask: _" How can I love you better today?" _

That's who Charlie really was. _That 's who I fell in love with. _

**And I want to tell you that story, Peter. **

We met at what I thought was a job interview.

Charlie messaged me in August of 2018 -- very Charlie-like -- short, direct, and bold:

_" Hey, I need to meet with you. Urgently." _

I thought it was about a position with Turning Point. It wasn't.

He took me to Bill's Burgers in NYC. I thought I was about to be grilled for a role... and instead, I was grilled about Aristotle, theology, the Constitution, and how I saw my future.

Three and a half hours of deep conversation, and by the end of it, I still didn't know what to think.

**Then Charlie looked at me and said: **

_**" I'm not going to hire you. I'm going to date you." **_

I froze. I told him, "Maybe we should just be friends first."

He didn't skip a beat: _" I have enough friends." _

That was Charlie.

Clarity. Conviction. A heart that always knew exactly what it wanted. And completely unshakable when he knew what was right.

God knew I needed someone who would say, "I'm not playing games. I'm not going to play with your heart. I'm a loyal person. I'm a good person. I'm a God-fearing person. I want to date you."

**God just knew that I needed someone like that. And He said, "Here's Charlie." **

**He loved God. He loved me and our family. He loved America. He loved this movement. **

**Charlie also believed in you, Peter. **

He believed in the students who had never heard the truth before.

He believed in the greatness of America -- even when things were dark or felt hopeless to us all.

Charlie was a father, a husband, a leader, and a warrior.

But above all, Charlie was obedient...

Obedient to God. To his conscience. To the mission placed on his heart.

**Charlie and I didn 't just build a life together -- _we built a calling. _**

And now...

**I don 't just bear his calling -- I will lead. **

**I will lead the movement he built forward, in Charlie 's name and for God's glory. **

_**"And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' Then I said, 'Here I am! Send me.' " **_ _**~ Isaiah 6:8 ** _
**Charlie answered that call every day of his life. Now, it 's my turn. **

And if you're reading this -- _maybe it 's yours, too. _

We are all being called.

To serve. To love boldly. To stand. To fight for what matters.

Because Charlie's life was not taken in vain.

The evil that tried to silence him has only made his voice louder.

We will carry the torch, Peter.

Together.

And the mission Charlie started -- it will become greater than we ever imagined.

Because God is not done.

And neither are we.

With faith, love, strength, and unshakable hope...

Just Charlie. _In his element. _

_Because this was Charlie at the height of everything he lived for -- his purpose, his calling, his mission... _

** **

It was about a man laying down his life, every single day, for something eternal.

**Charlie, I miss you. **

_**" Well done, my good and faithful servant." **_

**And I promise... **

Running for Congress and challenging the bipartisan corporate corruption in Washington led me to [discover](https://substack.com/redirect/5f8a5c42-0717-4ed1-8ea9-0990449d5063?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) how little democracy means in the U.S. I was forced to confront the role of the press in [building](https://substack.com/redirect/8c83fa7d-1d19-4972-b635-6b1b1b687754?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) deferential [cults](https://substack.com/redirect/5e0a2a9c-f79b-4799-a907-32875bf5f566?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of personality and [blocking](https://substack.com/redirect/7d6b4246-24ef-4fb2-becf-d2966440faf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) rare public debate, as well as the disturbing [propensity](https://substack.com/redirect/f5606486-a431-4beb-a619-9d38f78e2c0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of even self-described "progressives" and "socialists" in blue cities towards [white supremacy](https://substack.com/redirect/c0241ebc-9fba-4589-8f5d-bee587c8bb3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Put simply, trying to help defend the future ended my career, and sent me to the mountains to [start](https://substack.com/redirect/c7f6d750-9661-472b-9060-5d196815a0d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new life in 2022.
I felt surprised this week to find myself silenced once again.

### **Who needs government to suppress speech?**
Monday morning, I posted a link to [my latest article & podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/0b1c0900-d8f2-456c-891b-0667eef6d7d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a group chat thread organized by one of my employers, through which employees have been encouraged to share memes, invitations to social events, and announcements.
Several colleagues--all white men of a certain age--chimed in immediately to express a shared concern. They wanted not to be confronted by politics, and urged for the chat to be closed to any related discussions.
The immediacy of their responses surprised me, since the thread had been silent for a few days.
It also felt ironic, since the subject of my post was how the constitutional crisis which we are now all living through was made possible by relatively comfortable Americans ignoring the crises of their less comfortable neighbors. Ultimately, it simply paraphrased Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. and applied [his analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/e9897699-d04b-4e19-9036-f4e1f6bd8f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the present.
Maybe I shouldn't be so surprised at the reaction to my post, given the [reaction to his voice](https://substack.com/redirect/dd78089a-c8a5-40f0-8305-32d4caf857e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
### **Observing patterns**
It seems predictable that the many messages of support I received yesterday would come in private, and doubly ironic that they would disproportionately come from fellow workers who had immigrated to the U.S.
Meanwhile, the only other voices chiming in on the (not exactly, but at least relatively more public) group thread all supported calls to exclude speech examining politics.
A manager soon stepped in to embrace that invitation, declaring the thread off-limits to political discussion. They were, however, kind enough to reach out--privately--to express support, and sympathy for my perspective.
Beyond observing the dynamic of colleagues choosing to ignore current events, I also casually lamented the loss of an arena through which we used to be able to inform each other. But while that lament was casual, it points to a real issue with broader relevance.
We are all growing increasingly aware of our government's various attempts at suppressing constitutionally protected expression. From agencies [ignoring](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d2e11a-ba40-465b-bd1d-613950f73bef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) court orders and [deporting](https://substack.com/redirect/2606c851-e0cd-49a8-8ae0-50c8dfb2536a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) student dissidents, to the president himself seeking to force insightful [comedians](https://substack.com/redirect/c9017123-0229-448d-b44e-32b13e418fc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) off the air and deploying ICE goon squads around the country to [assault](https://substack.com/redirect/63076fa5-01db-44b7-b313-7ea7b397de76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) activists peacefully defending human rights in their communities, the whole has already grown worse than the sum of its parts.
What most disappointed me about the reaction from my colleagues was witnessing the tendency for fascism to find support not only in government, but also in culture.
That is the point at which it grows especially pernicious. And we're already there, even in a mountain town seemingly far from the cultural flashpoints that have divided the rest of the U.S.

To the extent my experience reflected grassroots censorship enforced within civil society, it resembles the pattern of newspapers owners [sacrificing](https://substack.com/redirect/7180d423-7a9e-4ac3-9419-312493638156?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) editorial independence in order to curry favor with our leaders, or corporate executives to silence critics of the regime.
### **A victory revealing defeat**
I'm as grateful as anyone else that Jimmy Kimmel's late night show has been [restored](https://substack.com/redirect/c95ede39-5d75-4b1d-9c4a-70e58f35cc38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and will return to the air this evening. But it's going to take a lot more than that to get me to celebrate.
On the one hand, the restoration of Kimmel's show confirmed the power of consumer boycotts. Like any number of collective action strategies, boycotts offer influence beyond what we can each attain as individuals.
One of the tragedies of this political moment is that so many institutions that immediately capitulated to the right wing don't have consumer-facing operations vulnerable to similar strategies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0aec8e78-b89a-427d-870b-758b57c50951?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For instance, the [law firms that bent their knees](https://substack.com/redirect/46d8586e-815f-435f-b0e7-192762d4f14c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Trump tend to serve businesses, more than consumers. Meanwhile, [compliant universities](https://substack.com/redirect/e103a10e-6953-49f6-81fb-6c742970abd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) serve any number of stakeholders, from faculty and students to government agencies and corporate employers--but none (except for potential applicants) situated to stage a boycott.
A greater tragedy of this political moment is the one that prompted the post I tried to share with my colleagues.

Today's widespread indignation--from conservatives lamenting an assassination, as well as liberals responding to the cancellation of comedians, proves his point.](https://substack.com/redirect/0b1c0900-d8f2-456c-891b-0667eef6d7d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

I'm glad the boycott worked, and so relatively immediately, at that.
On the other hand, it is dejecting to watch so many liberals grow prompted to outrage and mobilization only due to the suspension of a wealthy white comedian's program--not by an ongoing genocide in Gaza, nor by an accelerating climate catastrophe destroying life around the world, nor by arbitrary state violence leaving their Black neighbors dead at alarming rates.
Two men were [lynched in Mississippi](https://substack.com/redirect/25f73632-9f62-4c89-b971-9cef100a0a9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week, but that was not what drove America's liberal masses to outrage. To be fair, there is no particular institution to boycott in response to those events, but the scale of online discussion concerning Kimmel dwarfed that addressing the murder of Trey Reed.
On the one hand, this saga shows the power of collective action. On the other hand, it also reveals the limits of solidarity.
Why does Kimmel's show matter so much more to so many observers than Reed's life?
### **A multigenerational struggle**
When Dr. King [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/f22ecdca-5ffb-46d1-9b66-de74d762479d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about the unwillingness of "the White moderate" to take action in solidarity with people seeking long overdue justice, he observed an unfortunate tendency rooted in repeated _choices_ to ignore. The colleagues responding to my post this week reflected precisely the patterns that Dr. King observed roughly 70 years ago.
Since his era, the combined weight of similar choices have led an entire civilization to such pervasive [ignorance](https://substack.com/redirect/b5e375a1-bebb-4095-b5f8-970d6ab0d17d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that we have shot ourselves in the collective feet--effectively shooting the future in the face at the same time.
Who could ever have thought that so many Americans would reduce themselves to [emulating](https://substack.com/redirect/ef3d2865-2c70-4ae7-94f1-56e96fb72ae4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Dick Cheney?

clean_body: Listen now (9 mins) | I was silenced once in retaliation for raising my voice in public, before being silenced again this week when raising it privately | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | ]() | | I was silenced once in retaliation for raising my voice in public, before being silenced again this week when raising it privately | | | Sep 24| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | Running for Congress and challenging the bipartisan corporate corruption in Washington led me to how little democracy means in the U.S. I was forced to confront the role of the press in deferential of personality and rare public debate, as well as the disturbing of even self-described "progressives" and "socialists" in blue cities towards . Put simply, trying to help defend the future ended my career, and sent me to the mountains to a new life in 2022. I felt surprised this week to find myself silenced once again. Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! You can inform and inspire your friends by sharing this post. Who needs government to suppress speech? Monday morning, I posted a link to in a group chat thread organized by one of my employers, through which employees have been encouraged to share memes, invitations to social events, and announcements. Several colleagues--all white men of a certain age--chimed in immediately to express a shared concern. They wanted not to be confronted by politics, and urged for the chat to be closed to any related discussions. The immediacy of their responses surprised me, since the thread had been silent for a few days. It also felt ironic, since the subject of my post was how the constitutional crisis which we are now all living through was made possible by relatively comfortable Americans ignoring the crises of their less comfortable neighbors. Ultimately, it simply paraphrased Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. and applied to the present. Maybe I shouldn't be so surprised at the reaction to my post, given the . Observing patterns It seems predictable that the many messages of support I received yesterday would come in private, and doubly ironic that they would disproportionately come from fellow workers who had immigrated to the U.S. Meanwhile, the only other voices chiming in on the (not exactly, but at least relatively more public) group thread all supported calls to exclude speech examining politics. A manager soon stepped in to embrace that invitation, declaring the thread off-limits to political discussion. They were, however, kind enough to reach out--privately--to express support, and sympathy for my perspective. Beyond observing the dynamic of colleagues choosing to ignore current events, I also casually lamented the loss of an arena through which we used to be able to inform each other. But while that lament was casual, it points to a real issue with broader relevance. We are all growing increasingly aware of our government's various attempts at suppressing constitutionally protected expression. From agencies court orders and student dissidents, to the president himself seeking to force insightful off the air and deploying ICE goon squads around the country to activists peacefully defending human rights in their communities, the whole has already grown worse than the sum of its parts. What most disappointed me about the reaction from my colleagues was witnessing the tendency for fascism to find support not only in government, but also in culture. That is the point at which it grows especially pernicious. And we're already there, even in a mountain town seemingly far from the cultural flashpoints that have divided the rest of the U.S. Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts,sign up for a free subscription! To support my work defending democracy and exposing corruption, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. To the extent my experience reflected grassroots censorship enforced within civil society, it resembles the pattern of newspapers owners editorial independence in order to curry favor with our leaders, or corporate executives to silence critics of the regime. A victory revealing defeat I'm as grateful as anyone else that Jimmy Kimmel's late night show has been and will return to the air this evening. But it's going to take a lot more than that to get me to celebrate. On the one hand, the restoration of Kimmel's show confirmed the power of consumer boycotts. Like any number of collective action strategies, boycotts offer influence beyond what we can each attain as individuals. One of the tragedies of this political moment is that so many institutions that immediately capitulated to the right wing don't have consumer-facing operations vulnerable to similar strategies. | | ---|---|--- For instance, the to Trump tend to serve businesses, more than consumers. Meanwhile, serve any number of stakeholders, from faculty and students to government agencies and corporate employers--but none (except for potential applicants) situated to stage a boycott. A greater tragedy of this political moment is the one that prompted the post I tried to share with my colleagues. | | | | ---|---|--- | Sep 20 | I'm glad the boycott worked, and so relatively immediately, at that. On the other hand, it is dejecting to watch so many liberals grow prompted to outrage and mobilization only due to the suspension of a wealthy white comedian's program--not by an ongoing genocide in Gaza, nor by an accelerating climate catastrophe destroying life around the world, nor by arbitrary state violence leaving their Black neighbors dead at alarming rates. Two men were last week, but that was not what drove America's liberal masses to outrage. To be fair, there is no particular institution to boycott in response to those events, but the scale of online discussion concerning Kimmel dwarfed that addressing the murder of Trey Reed. On the one hand, this saga shows the power of collective action. On the other hand, it also reveals the limits of solidarity. Why does Kimmel's show matter so much more to so many observers than Reed's life? A multigenerational struggle** When Dr. King about the unwillingness of "the White moderate" to take action in solidarity with people seeking long overdue justice, he observed an unfortunate tendency rooted in repeated choices to ignore. The colleagues responding to my post this week reflected precisely the patterns that Dr. King observed roughly 70 years ago. Since his era, the combined weight of similar choices have led an entire civilization to such pervasive that we have shot ourselves in the collective feet--effectively shooting the future in the face at the same time. Who could ever have thought that so many Americans would reduce themselves to Dick Cheney? Paid subscribers can access an additional section reporting on some updates relating to previous posts. I wrote in 2023 about how civil society in the U.S. could force an end to the Israeli genocide in Gaza, before a pair of more recent updates this year. Yesterday, a European country demonstrated the strategy I suggested in 2023, which seems to have led a substantial number of new readers to my writing... name: Erika Kirk, Turning Point USA
subject: This is the story of Charlie I want to tell
body:
I miss him. Every day.
I don’t know how else to begin except with this:

[ ](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=959c68867e9f43829225071fdf06d794&_e=tRVr_syKeHm4Jn3nevsZgeM2LD0A0_sXCzPWBE46GXRE5FLMy4sV1B-ZJdCypCc9pKXfzBrv3RAgMk7Aur2lUsXogLLAMhmKtXtNAONJFtkmdUN-0_jEG6DyKhf5hH-QUDhOFLF4PtYnCD-l-QaD1qUQVWtnShT2lXjpfH4qHslKKmiL-bN9akMtCiM6spwz13TwGUA8k1HO_06fSEg256mJFrYsDQOEijvJrDXgt_OrhJcfxJ4LVJRW8rS9XNGotA9SJKVrgkktXh_hc0NXSaoY4dSW1XZxwtUFaUQcNLtLd_4A4-jY1jXarD2rXlpqP6O83S41mKs7lTWf74woLw7P8jOJBFMpO-FBNUeSXN-xHpx4P6et95BsDTCHsIUDdL8Z4L3l9vFB4MzcUO1NdLhQLCltS0rJAJYtAg7lbU3PMolPX92MGO4r5VYlULZ_H7MtM12yX1uwtWCt6n_HyTvfOjQ2KJAyM3b49KuPWR_BSUOWB3agEvH-vlEuZvc-E4U9W6tzvH0SoEjy5227G6chMHdMVvvU8if6ifmE-sJCsowQ4scMgMExBFFssG-iloeWqAl-Ed9bVWXYziIBS-MfldhOdn1HkGlTg4oHAlZ0-R8IPgVsM5MuN7agxUErG-vZ2ODendoS2k_f5ghZc5t6qNjpyTYYzl5IfGpguaxtH5VHf_00_JTjfyAbON7ekFuOPZPXsgHlgv2xnspsFw%3D%3D) | Peter, I don't know how else to begin except with this:

**_I miss him. _**

Every breath. Every heartbeat. Every memory I now replay in my mind... I miss him.

My husband, Charlie Kirk, was the love of my life.

You may know him as a fighter for freedom. A warrior for truth. The founder of Turning Point USA. The host of a nationally syndicated radio show. A bold conservative voice that gave courage to a generation.

But to me... _He was just Charlie._
---
[ ](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=959c68867e9f43829225071fdf06d794&_e=tRVr_syKeHm4Jn3nevsZgeM2LD0A0_sXCzPWBE46GXRE5FLMy4sV1B-ZJdCypCc9pKXfzBrv3RAgMk7Aur2lUsXogLLAMhmKtXtNAONJFtkmdUN-0_jEG6DyKhf5hH-QUDhOFLF4PtYnCD-l-QaD1qUQVWtnShT2lXjpfH4qHslKKmiL-bN9akMtCiM6spwz13TwGUA8k1HO_06fSEg256mJFrYsDQOEijvJrDXgt_OrhJcfxJ4LVJRW8rS9XNGowIWEP-1ScKEisGRdcpdXyZ2A9jfklvGwgBK8eI0fDjlaNHLzypErPoeKfQEwVMMRS8LlmUfyMhtI8MG5Si3OlpdDm6LEaQQ2EOfsVJkVjCSuHd-9WwPKldruFre648CKQ4QXXPS5uVLV4yHeiSWS6WrrWOikd-AjLcGRAVmI79TsDn6KmkqyYhYLALCx1XLQ7teQ4VVJq_D5IpB5SAkdVb0yC4HDvxxrfTKBuxmYalKR6N6iO14z5HThA-8LEOXRXVlEWcC1o_8MQtT432x9EHxcx8wam6ICWzgNl40hZNKqpSlATT-XiW9mumWT0tjslhuCABNffQaTbaZUAy5pdTrmB37QxZindxxzg3AuYVNn_uL8Q6FFoYD1k8W2Om2XEMVpSGfKklAPqcudKjUNdcl6MHbPJoWDcvx5GCYkqtQtDu7Ej4V4OOCLHwsGaARpJ0_357utgR1Xp5SytlEYZA%3D%3D)
He was my best friend. The father of our two precious babies. The man who made me laugh when the world felt too heavy.

The man who, every single morning without fail, would look at me and ask: _" How can I love you better today?" _

That's who Charlie really was. _That 's who I fell in love with. _

**And I want to tell you that story, Peter. **

We met at what I thought was a job interview.

Charlie messaged me in August of 2018 -- very Charlie-like -- short, direct, and bold:

_" Hey, I need to meet with you. Urgently." _

I thought it was about a position with Turning Point. It wasn't.

He took me to Bill's Burgers in NYC. I thought I was about to be grilled for a role... and instead, I was grilled about Aristotle, theology, the Constitution, and how I saw my future.

Three and a half hours of deep conversation, and by the end of it, I still didn't know what to think.

**Then Charlie looked at me and said: **

_**" I'm not going to hire you. I'm going to date you." **_

I froze. I told him, "Maybe we should just be friends first."

He didn't skip a beat: _" I have enough friends." _

That was Charlie.

Clarity. Conviction. A heart that always knew exactly what it wanted. And completely unshakable when he knew what was right.

God knew I needed someone who would say, "I'm not playing games. I'm not going to play with your heart. I'm a loyal person. I'm a good person. I'm a God-fearing person. I want to date you."

**God just knew that I needed someone like that. And He said, "Here's Charlie." **

We fell fast -- and we fell deep.

It wasn't glamorous. Our lives were chaotic. Travel, pressure, early mornings, and late nights.

_But we understood each other... _

Charlie had found his mission. And I had found mine -- _to stand by his side. _

It's how I first met him -- _driven, intense, humble, and joyful in the simplest moments. _

Just Charlie. _In his element. _

I remembered the early days of dating, us on a basketball court. No lights, no crowd, no noise -- just the sound of sneakers on pavement.

We bonded over how Jordan was the GOAT, and he told me about his basketball days in high school and I told him about my basketball days in college.

He wore a red bracelet on his wrist that read: _**" Work harder. Be better." **_

He never took it off. Until one day, a student came up to him after a speech and asked about it. Charlie slipped it off and gave it to them.

That was who he was. He saw greatness in others, _even when they couldn 't yet see it in themselves. _

**That 's what I see in this photo -- _Greatness. _**

**To me, this is Charlie 's "Jordan" photo. **

_Because this was his prime... _

_Because this was Charlie at the height of everything he lived for -- his purpose, his calling, his mission... _

He trained his whole life for this exact moment, the moment he'd be called home.

He gave it everything. Mind. Body. Soul.

**Because it 's alive in me. It's alive in our children. It's alive in the millions he's inspired. **
** **
**And if you 're reading this, I know it's alive in you, too. **

Peter, Charlie's life -- it was so much bigger than politics...

It was about a man laying down his life, every single day, for something eternal.

And now, he's running his race where it really counts -- _where it never ends. _

**Charlie, I miss you. **

I pray you're having the most amazing time in Heaven.

And Charlie, baby, I promise I will never let your legacy slow or go silent.

I promise I'll make Turning Point USA the biggest thing that this nation has ever seen. I promise.

I love you, baby. Rest in the arms of our Lord as he blankets you with the words I know your heart _always_ strived to hear:

_**" Well done, my good and faithful servant." **_

You lived life well. You earned it.

**And I promise... **

**I 'll carry the torch you lit from here. _We 'll all carry it from here. _**

**" University of Texas sets records for enrollment, applications, retention," **Austin American-Statesman's **Lily Kepner** \-- "The**** University of Texas -- again -- is breaking enrollment, application and retention records as it kicks off its 2025 academic year, according to a report by the school.

This fall, an all-time high of 55,000 students enrolled for class at the 40 Acres,**** with a 7.5% increase for first-time college students at 9,900 incoming freshmen.

Undergraduate enrollment also increased, climbing to 44,314 students. The freshmen were selected from a pool of an all-time high 90,690 applicants, nearly 18,000 -- or 25% -- more than the previous year and 51% more since 2022.

The first-year retention rate**** of 97.1% is also the highest ever, a UT news release said,**** and significantly higher than the national average**** of about 77%, according to the National Student Clearinghouse Research Center. Four-year retention**** at UT increased to 75.7% from 75% in fall 2024.

UT also awarded 576 more degrees than the previous year at 15,963, the highest amount the institution has conferred in a year.

"We are educating more students than at any time in our University's history, and most importantly, we are doing it while maintaining our standard of academic excellence," UT President **Jim Davis** said in a news**** release last week. "That is our commitment as the public flagship university in Texas. I am proud of our students for their achievements and grateful to our faculty and staff for their hard work in support of our students' academic experience."

The university credits the high-demand to greater affordability and student performance, as well as its reputation for excellence.

U.S. News & World Reports ranked UT the 30th best college in the nation and seventh**** best public school, as well as the top public university in Texas. But its affordability initiatives are a key part of its attractiveness to students.

Texas full-time undergraduates paid $3,852 for the 2024-2025 academic year, nearly a third of the average full tuition price, $11,823. Net-tuition was even less for incoming full-time freshman, who paid $2,582 on average that year, according to the news release.

This is also the first batch of students benefiting from the UT System's increased investment in its Promise Plus initiative, where the system committed to covering tuition for any student from a household with an adjusted total combined income of $100,000 or less.

At UT, this means 12,200 undergraduate students are attending tuition-free this year, or**** 4,575 more students than in 2024, when the threshold for free tuition was $65,000 and about 27.5% of its undergraduate class.

An additional 1,500 students from households with less than $125,000 adjusted gross income are receiving subsidized tuition at UT, the university said, through its Texas Advanced Commitment that**** offers tuition support for about a third of its undergraduate students.

UT also provides financial support for housing through**** its Presidential Scholarship, which is now in its third year.

More than 22% of undergraduate students are first-generation students, meaning**** they are the first in their families to go to college. The more than 10,000 such**** students is an increase from 2023 when 9,015 students were first generation, but a slightly smaller total percentage of students." TOP NEWS " University of Texas sets records for enrollment, applications, retention," Austin American-Statesman's Lily Kepner \-- "The University of Texas -- again -- is breaking enrollment, application and retention records as it kicks off its 2025 academic year, according to a report by the school. This fall, an all-time high of 55,000 students enrolled for class at the 40 Acres, with a 7.5% increase for first-time college students at 9,900 incoming freshmen. Undergraduate enrollment also increased, climbing to 44,314 students. The freshmen were selected from a pool of an all-time high 90,690 applicants, nearly 18,000 -- or 25% -- more than the previous year and 51% more since 2022. The first-year retention rate of 97.1% is also the highest ever, a UT news release said, and significantly higher than the national average of about 77%, according to the National Student Clearinghouse Research Center. Four-year retention at UT increased to 75.7% from 75% in fall 2024. UT also awarded 576 more degrees than the previous year at 15,963, the highest amount the institution has conferred in a year. "We are educating more students than at any time in our University's history, and most importantly, we are doing it while maintaining our standard of academic excellence," UT President Jim Davis said in a news release last week. "That is our commitment as the public flagship university in Texas. I am proud of our students for their achievements and grateful to our faculty and staff for their hard work in support of our students' academic experience." The university credits the high-demand to greater affordability and student performance, as well as its reputation for excellence. U.S. News & World Reports ranked UT the 30th best college in the nation and seventh best public school, as well as the top public university in Texas. But its affordability initiatives are a key part of its attractiveness to students. Texas full-time undergraduates paid $3,852 for the 2024-2025 academic year, nearly a third of the average full tuition price, $11,823. Net-tuition was even less for incoming full-time freshman, who paid $2,582 on average that year, according to the news release. This is also the first batch of students benefiting from the UT System's increased investment in its Promise Plus initiative, where the system committed to covering tuition for any student from a household with an adjusted total combined income of $100,000 or less. At UT, this means 12,200 undergraduate students are attending tuition-free this year, or 4,575 more students than in 2024, when the threshold for free tuition was $65,000 and about 27.5% of its undergraduate class. An additional 1,500 students from households with less than $125,000 adjusted gross income are receiving subsidized tuition at UT, the university said, through its Texas Advanced Commitment that offers tuition support for about a third of its undergraduate students. UT also provides financial support for housing through its Presidential Scholarship, which is now in its third year. More than 22% of undergraduate students are first-generation students, meaning they are the first in their families to go to college. The more than 10,000 such students is an increase from 2023 when 9,015 students were first generation, but a slightly smaller total percentage of students." ## Secret Service Busts Big Telecom Threat
The Secret Service uncovered a [massive illegal telecom network](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZD2yGzMeAgeXkM2lFyJjmsG3xkZ2MyP-fsX-wmYllfT0qv49x6cLMaTXX7eR5SWPiT41EjOVkcux7UeqO5Ffz3zwMZF3ydOIEjuQPaAeZxfiOepmtgsRUtuQVaZ7GPlo1aNZ7R17pf20mKlHY6TpDLll1mrRd616r5pgL5rsUSspO2VuJEljZ2Tf-q6TkxFa0hw4l9v_HBKvtMQzv6ncfN6aaFfmvYr2j8BB4JDOPVe-KoHDBRY4yP7KrcDhqHDtEzhU8oUYKpV38ARLDrHCHjMDZ5hDLcfOkE4PnmKERPzJ5Qt4LeSYEhwJXpSouAiuVtqmeAocmmLn_RNiDPV-ab82F-KPJv_q27fF7wAAAP__Le6OnA) near the UN General Assembly meeting in New York. Officials say it could have caused “catastrophic” disruptions if activated. Agents seized more than [300 SIM servers and over 100,000 SIM cards](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkE3SnSAURFeDMyy8QnwOGGTi7GWaoYVwfZLwY8FVy92nTLKDbwGn-3T_fM9v44NPnx8moqY1zwmvGpAIy0zliPuR6o5otzsfdCxoTbI4gwDFxchBzs74cM-ycXpFBOwb1N2gXoN49d2r2bSUIxgQUnTLMHbWuNG8Vte7xSgFRvaN10-aGEF2QqhuaFGgBDWIsbdKiWVgUqDzlEv7K_tEG67hzieW1ubYBL0R7ZX13xlMDKbrutqKtiBVLKe32H7yyWB6ZpWcI4OpYEBTsTKYnmYGkxgZTEfl_0D-n-TO12gSBazcx-gTJuKEAW2O8UjeGvI5VU5bQUM84cXvXH43Rbv98iH4-u1x_0Tjw19X-tLBp4Y_AQAA___0KpL8), which officials say could have been used to jam 911 calls, knock out cell towers, or flood networks with up to 30 million text messages per minute. Similar setups have reportedly been found in California and the Midwest. While no direct plot against the UN General Assembly has been identified, officials are treating the case as a major security threat.

## Irving-Based Nexstar Still Preempting Kimmel

## Eli Lilly to Build $6.5B Plant in Houston
Eli Lilly, a multinational drug manufacturer based in Indianapolis, announced it will [build a $6.5 billion plant](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAUhZ8Gu-sAYsCCIo1dUu6WDspV2UVwgMT49jtm9g3-9t4z35zv_H4MD-O8C8vTbKjLZ45DwCN7LAXTcGvHNb5yiWH3JpQ8JTyOmLZl4JS3QDvgYrDG-XMQldUjtR2rUDPZKsmYbGS16hGnjjJqlZmsapSxjVQzcqq4VJYzWzl9wWjHBWOUM1ELIwzrmGKtojjLkQiK1pWY6rJiwY_Jsz_jG1M9xa3yei1lz6S5E94T3h_HUW85XD_CewzwyoT3Wwx4Et7HsmK67t6Bd96fsLvpb4b_mjDHBDdoR_gKQ1lNgcN5D2NyYQEBlFL4E8eLaRLc7-zZPX-5Kmm7XzmXb5IIumzG-W-98rNR35r_CwAA__8Ne4tJ) in Houston to boost production of drugs administered in pill form, including its experimental GLP-1 obesity drug orforglipron. The Houston plant—the [second of four](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAQx58GOwwgiBYU29jdbbc0gKgkIxiYczy-_cbzCrebZGZ-_49_P_OPjRDT9tceweBnzXMKV4WAGMrcK7fnV8WcTrAJqy_hunI5tlkwoSgbqZDzYiPcs2wW49gy8iYYrtWgOdedbnaj7Wi9E6LzrNeWM6cC6zVXTo-q82FoonlgbBSScya4bKWVlo984GpgYdWOSBaWiLm0uAcMH1tXuPM7lNbnowGzI56VdH-ImIiYrutqfXL-WRIxPWwiJjY-c0fEFCBSiAA3fTJV2p85JlTURYCYE_0K0MOm12o9vkpM2_cS6ZoLzS7UiDc9I0C74wFNMct5Pb-110Sy7bARvsbwd3W-jfgfAAD__z17igU) the company plans to announce this year—is part of a $27 billion commitment to U.S. manufacturing capacity announced in February. The investment could insulate the company from tariffs on imported pharmaceuticals. "_Our new Houston site will enhance Lilly's ability to manufacture orforglipron at scale and, if approved, help fulfill the medicine's potential as an obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment_ ," Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks said in a statement. The facility is expected to be operational [within five years](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuS2zAMQE9DdfSQsGxZBYs07DZtSg0_sMUEIjwU1lzfPqPM3iAdCsx7D_j1sXyEQqU-foYNnXzdeanYd0IRbMv1Elf-3IXrk0KVPTXsndv2WMDARZtZw7jkUOi9jEN20eTZDujsdLlN1k7naVhdiBAntCFeAc8xXyFHAxky3tI8wWyH4g6YmWG01oAdT2MYg53tzV5uBu9TVKPBXITbSVYU_Ar7nd78wnZKvA3kVpHnrs4_FHgFvvd-SlTSH_hOP7YU-OMsBZ44BVLgD6cCb-ZjPivwj4NYuekQI4toYR1q5c-aUG_hNzeNiStvJemMLyR-blhF9yKrRiqaCtFbl6q_tQr80Fx-9kJU9uukRvPYQqF_0fJ_r345-BsAAP__LQaU4w) and create 615 permanent jobs.

The Houston plant—the the company plans to announce this year—is part of a $27 billion commitment to U.S. manufacturing capacity announced in February. "Our new Houston site will enhance Lilly's ability to manufacture orforglipron at scale and, if approved, help fulfill the medicine's potential as an obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment ," Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks said in a statement. clean_body: Democrats have been caught completely off guard in the most important election of 2025 and are being outspent 10-1. We are now on track for a catastrophic defeat. | | | | | == | Peter, The disaster we've been warning about for months is materializing before our eyes. The National Republican Party has caught Democrats completely off guard and has launched a daring lightning blitz in an obscure but critically important judicial election in Pennsylvania that we thought we had in the bag. The race is the November 2025, Pennsylvania Supreme Court Election and if Democrats lose here we will never win Pennsylvania in an election again, not in 2026 and not in 2028 \- 19 electoral college votes squandered. These judicial races typically garner zero attention and are often ignored by the national parties but with the courts being one of the only things standing in the way of Trump's agenda we knew this year it would be different... | | == | | | | For months we rang the alarm that MAGA was going all out to win this race but no one listened. Now the GOP has broken through and is making this the most expensive Supreme Court election in American history. Democrats have been caught completely off guard and are being outspent 10-1. We are now on track for a catastrophic defeat. This was nothing short of an ambush, and Defend Our Courts, one of the only Democratic orgs holding the line, is scrambling to contain the GOP's breakthrough. To plug the gaps in our lines we've spent nearly our entire field budget, which was supposed to last until November, to hire hundreds of new rapid response canvassers. Peter, I don't even know how to begin to put into words the loss I am feeling... but this isn't about me. **Today, tomorrow, next week -- they're all about Charlie. ** Because Charlie was truly one of the best men I'll ever know. He changed the direction of this nation. He was a leader, a fighter, and a man whose character and conviction were rare. Too rare. He was an inspiration to millions around the world. **To me, Charlie was a little brother.** That honor I will carry with me forever.

I'm heartbroken knowing his death will leave a hole in the heart of our nation.... and an even larger one in my life. Charlie may no longer stand beside me -- to remind me to push on when things get tough. _But his memory will._ _And I 'll make sure it does for this country he loved so well._ Charlie led a life of courage, strength, and conviction. **Now it 's time for me, for you, and for every patriot to stand up and fight for everything Charlie stood for. ** He poured every ounce of energy he had into saving this nation -- and he did that through Turning Point USA. No one fought harder than Charlie. It was his mission in life to give people the courage to speak up -- and he did that. And none of us will ever be silenced again. He fought for you and all America. name: Erika Kirk, Turning Point USA
subject: I miss him. Every day.
body:
| | |
---
Friend, I don’t know how else to begin except with this:

**_I miss him. _**

Every breath. Every heartbeat. Every memory I now replay in my mind... I miss him.

My husband, Charlie Kirk, was the love of my life.

You may know him as a fighter for freedom. A warrior for truth. The founder of Turning Point USA. The host of a nationally syndicated radio show. A bold conservative voice that gave courage to a generation.

But to me... _He was just Charlie._
---
---
He was my best friend. The father of our two precious babies. The man who made me laugh when the world felt too heavy.

The man who, every single morning without fail, would look at me and ask: _“How can I love you better today?” _

That’s who Charlie really was. _That’s who I fell in love with. _

**And I want to tell you that story, friend. **

We met at what I thought was a job interview.

Charlie messaged me in August of 2018 — very Charlie-like — short, direct, and bold:

_“Hey, I need to meet with you. Urgently.” _

I thought it was about a position with Turning Point. It wasn’t.

He took me to Bill’s Burgers in NYC. I thought I was about to be grilled for a role... and instead, I was grilled about Aristotle, theology, the Constitution, and how I saw my future.

Three and a half hours of deep conversation, and by the end of it, I still didn’t know what to think.

**Then Charlie looked at me and said: **

_**“I’m not going to hire you. I’m going to date you.” **_

I froze. I told him, “Maybe we should just be friends first.”

He didn’t skip a beat: _“I have enough friends.” _

That was Charlie.

Clarity. Conviction. A heart that always knew exactly what it wanted. And completely unshakable when he knew what was right.

God knew I needed someone who would say, “I'm not playing games. I'm not going to play with your heart. I'm a loyal person. I'm a good person. I'm a God-fearing person. I want to date you.”

**God just knew that I needed someone like that. And He said, "Here's Charlie." **

We fell fast — and we fell deep.

It wasn’t glamorous. Our lives were chaotic. Travel, pressure, early mornings, and late nights.

_But we understood each other... _

Charlie had found his mission. And I had found mine — _to stand by his side. _
---
---
**He loved God. He loved me and our family. He loved America. He loved this movement. **

**Charlie also believed in you, patriot. **

He believed in the students who had never heard the truth before.

He believed in the greatness of America — even when things were dark or felt hopeless to us all.

Charlie was a father, a husband, a leader, and a warrior.

But above all, Charlie was obedient...

Obedient to God. To his conscience. To the mission placed on his heart.

**Charlie and I didn’t just build a life together — _we built a calling. _**

And now...

**I don’t just bear his calling — I will lead. **

**I will lead the movement he built forward, in Charlie’s name and for God’s glory. **
---
---
Before Charlie died, he often repeated one verse more than any other:
---
_**"And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' Then I said, 'Here I am! Send me.'”**_ _**~ Isaiah 6:8 ** _
---
**Charlie answered that call every day of his life. Now, it’s my turn. **

And if you’re reading this — _maybe it’s yours, too. _

We are all being called.

To serve. To love boldly. To stand. To fight for what matters.

Because Charlie’s life was not taken in vain.

The evil that tried to silence him has only made his voice louder.

We will carry the torch, friend.

Together.

And the mission Charlie started — it will become greater than we ever imagined.

Because God is not done.

And neither are we.

With faith, love, strength, and unshakable hope...
---
---
**Erika Kirk**
CEO & Chair of the Board Turning Point USA [_**Support Turning Point USA**_](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/be6o/?__vbtrk=MzIyMDcwOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzIyMDcwOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
---
**P.S.** Friend, you may have seen this already, but I want to share this with you anyways...

Charlie loved witnessing excellence. It’s why he loved sports so much.

He loved watching the best of the best perform at the level of greatness God intended for them.

Patriot, that’s why this photo... _One of the very last photos ever taken of Charlie... _

...Took the breath right out of my chest:
---
---
Because I know that look... _**I fell in love with that look.**_

He’s in athlete mode. Locked in. Dialed. Focused.

It’s how I first met him — _driven, intense, humble, and joyful in the simplest moments. _

Just Charlie. _In his element. _

I remembered the early days of dating, us on a basketball court. No lights, no crowd, no noise — just the sound of sneakers on pavement.

We bonded over how Jordan was the GOAT, and he told me about his basketball days in high school and I told him about my basketball days in college.

He wore a red bracelet on his wrist that read: _**“Work harder. Be better.” **_

He never took it off. Until one day, a student came up to him after a speech and asked about it. Charlie slipped it off and gave it to them.

That was who he was. He saw greatness in others, _even when they couldn’t yet see it in themselves. _

**That’s what I see in this photo — _Greatness. _**

**To me, this is Charlie’s “Jordan” photo. **

_Because this was his prime... _

_Because this was Charlie at the height of everything he lived for — his purpose, his calling, his mission... _

He trained his whole life for this exact moment, the moment he’d be called home.

He gave it everything. Mind. Body. Soul.

And now, this image is permanently etched in time, held in my heart, as I admire his greatness. _Forever._

Friend, I want you to know — his mission didn’t end. It won’t ever stop...

**Because it’s alive in me. It’s alive in our children. It’s alive in the millions he’s inspired. **
** **
**And if you’re reading this, I know it’s alive in you, too. **

Patriot, Charlie’s life — it was so much bigger than politics...

It was about a man laying down his life, every single day, for something eternal.

And now, he’s running his race where it really counts — _where it never ends. _

**Charlie, I miss you. **

I pray you’re having the most amazing time in Heaven.

And Charlie, baby, I promise I will never let your legacy slow or go silent.

I promise I'll make Turning Point USA the biggest thing that this nation has ever seen. I promise.

I love you, baby. Rest in the arms of our Lord as he blankets you with the words I know your heart _always_ strived to hear:

_**“Well done, my good and faithful servant.” **_

You lived life well. You earned it.

**And I promise... **

**I’ll carry the torch you lit from here._We’ll all carry it from here. _**
---

No lights, no crowd, no noise — just the sound of sneakers on pavement. We bonded over how Jordan was the GOAT, and he told me about his basketball days in high school and I told him about my basketball days in college. He wore a red bracelet on his wrist that read: “Work harder. Be better.” He never took it off. Until one day, a student came up to him after a speech and asked about it. Charlie slipped it off and gave it to them. That was who he was. He saw greatness in others, even when they couldn’t yet see it in themselves. That’s what I see in this photo — Greatness. To me, this is Charlie’s “Jordan” photo. Because this was his prime... Because this was Charlie at the height of everything he lived for — his purpose, his calling, his mission... He trained his whole life for this exact moment, the moment he’d be called home. He gave it everything. Mind. Body. Soul. And now, this image is permanently etched in time, held in my heart, as I admire his greatness. Forever. Friend, I want you to know — his mission didn’t end. It won’t ever stop... Because it’s alive in me. It’s alive in our children. It’s alive in the millions he’s inspired. And if you’re reading this, I know it’s alive in you, too. Patriot, Charlie’s life — it was so much bigger than politics... It was about a man laying down his life, every single day, for something eternal. And now, he’s running his race where it really counts — where it never ends. Charlie, I miss you. I pray you’re having the most amazing time in Heaven. And Charlie, baby, I promise I will never let your legacy slow or go silent. I promise I'll make Turning Point USA the biggest thing that this nation has ever seen. I promise. I love you, baby. Rest in the arms of our Lord as he blankets you with the words I know your heart always strived to hear: “Well done, my good and faithful servant.” You lived life well. You earned it. And I promise... I’ll carry the torch you lit from here.We’ll all carry it from here. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 | 215 N Payne Street, Alexandria, VA 22314

As someone who pays close attention to the news, I thought this past week was exhausting. I'm not going to relitigate all of it,1 because it's too easy to become a fatalist or a nihilist if you're only paying attention to the bad news.
So, for the next couple of posts, I'm going to focus instead on the positive, namely where I think Democrats have opportunities to change the narrative and win (or win back) voters.2
What I'll talk through in this post: the Trump administration is using the might of the federal government to come down hard on free speech. This is dangerous for America--and an opportunity for Democrats, if they choose to take it.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTc0MTgwMTQzLCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzU4NzE3NzY2LCJleHAiOjIwNzQyOTM3NjYsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.ADUNqdL3pO0U9J7_Xa6X8hUgEkzBmhuFuCQWb7X5VIk?)
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _Americans across the board feel less comfortable sharing their opinions and worry that the government is threatening their rights to free speech._
> * _That fear is especially present for Republicans and young men --creating an opportunity for Democrats to win back a demographic that's moving away from them._
> * _Democrats can own the issue of free speech, but it 'll require them to have difficult conversations in uncomfortable spaces. They haven't always done that well._
>

### Free speech had a rough week
In case you need a reminder, here's why this is salient:
* Trump threatened to [pull broadcast licenses for networks](https://substack.com/redirect/76210ad1-2509-4322-baef-8bfec8d3d53c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that are "against" him.
* Jimmy Kimmel, after making a joke related to Trump's reaction to Charlie Kirk's assassination, [had his show suspended by ABC](https://substack.com/redirect/834fec7e-f9f7-40d3-baac-ed118541a2a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). ([It returned last night](https://substack.com/redirect/f0130c25-b4ac-4851-a2e2-ef8e2325f695?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
* [Brendan Carr](https://substack.com/redirect/651bc4e5-9514-4e44-b9fa-3f517ecc35fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, [suggested that the government would pressure Disney](https://substack.com/redirect/b84113dc-7ce5-4383-bd02-365cb85d6016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (which owns ABC) to pull the show: "Frankly, when you see stuff like this--I mean, we can do this the easy way or the hard way."3

### Americans worry about losing their free speech
All of this is notable because Americans, for a while now, have become increasingly worried about their freedom of speech.4
In 2020, [46% of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/29736152-006a-4519-90f4-7988f78667a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) felt that they were less free to speak their mind than they once were. For context, only 13% of Americans felt that way _during the height of McCarthyism_ , a period famous for its suppression of free speech.
Five years on, people--especially men and Republicans--worry that they can't freely express their opinions.5
* [54% of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe8b655-ab28-44c0-bac2-c8fefc82a392?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) say that "the biggest threat to free speech is the government" vs. 25% who say that's not the case--and this poll was done back in February. A more recent survey (from Sept. 19) finds that Americans believe the [government is ](https://substack.com/redirect/2478d9f6-e60c-47d3-b2be-58ec73eee27f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[by far](https://substack.com/redirect/2478d9f6-e60c-47d3-b2be-58ec73eee27f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ the biggest threat](https://substack.com/redirect/2478d9f6-e60c-47d3-b2be-58ec73eee27f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to free speech.
* [59% of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe8b655-ab28-44c0-bac2-c8fefc82a392?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) say that "freedom of speech has become more limited during my lifetime," vs. 24% who say that's not the case. [63% of men (vs. 55% of women)](https://substack.com/redirect/4a0d2006-b2f4-4e41-8d72-60980bf9f890?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agree that free speech has become more limited, and [29% of men in college](https://substack.com/redirect/c3882551-5008-4223-88c6-9d289740e4b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) say that they're not comfortable sharing their political opinions (vs. 22% of women).6

Let's look more at [that February poll](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe8b655-ab28-44c0-bac2-c8fefc82a392?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), specifically focusing on partisan and gender divides. [60% of Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe8b655-ab28-44c0-bac2-c8fefc82a392?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), vs. 48% of Democrats, say that the government is the biggest threat to free speech.7 **69% of Republicans, vs. 48% of Democrats, say that free speech has become more limited in their lifetime**.
All of this is an opportunity for Democrats to create a wedge issue--especially for young men, [a group that moved hard towards Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/63bf7f52-c7d2-43cb-a336-b75a780f065b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the last election.8
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b9dffff0-0a14-4e5c-81bf-b401a3b6a556?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |

### Ted Cruz is right (?!)
I'd seen the reporting that [Ted Cruz forcefully came out against](https://substack.com/redirect/25d6535d-be93-4416-987c-9515790523ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) FCC Chairman Carr's "the easy way or the hard way" comment, but I wanted to listen for myself. Here's [the segment from his podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/a351350c-a193-4e9c-ade2-f258be13b82a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from the 21:11 mark.9
[| Jimmy Kimmel Fired-Was it Right & Should the FCC have Gotten Involved plus Trump Designates ANTIFA a Terrorist OrganizationPremiere NetworksEpisode
---|---](https://substack.com/redirect/cc1f2600-28c3-47e5-913b-c7e3607f594a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Cruz's logic for being against Carr's comment isn't necessarily mine. His take, basically, is that if Republicans weaponize the FCC now, just _imagine_ what the Democrats will do when they're in power!
But the broader point--that it's a very dangerous precedent for the government to threaten the revocation of broadcast licenses for stations whose programming they don't like--is a good one, and one where I agree with what Cruz is saying.
Ted Cruz here [isn't alone among Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/9f731462-f025-4f02-b766-234e57dcaa26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), by the way, and there are [lots of elected Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/0f0848f7-a2cc-453f-82bb-1f8b325cfb9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and right-leaning media personalities who are coming out and saying the same.
Some of this, I'm sure, is driven by the genuine philosophical belief that this is wrong. But these people (usually) aren't fools, and I think they see that the Trump administration is creating an opening for Democrats that wasn't there before.
### The left needs to own up to its mistakes on this issue
During the Biden years, a well-worn Republican talking point--[one that Ted Cruz](https://substack.com/redirect/fd23765d-1466-4653-aefb-63b50deede57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [himself used](https://substack.com/redirect/12ce963f-d4c0-408d-a771-1dde30ac2d72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--is that the Democrats, in cahoots with the largest tech companies, were censoring free speech. That's a bit of a different conversation, because tech companies aren't part of the government,10 but the point was clearly resonant.
Either way, in this context, **Democrats need to reckon with the fact that things were taken too far in the wake of the George Floyd protests in 2020** and into the early years of the Biden presidency.
* [As I noted earlier](https://substack.com/redirect/df74d111-cb84-4262-a020-67b19cb14298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it was a heated moment, and [almost half of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/29736152-006a-4519-90f4-7988f78667a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2020 felt less free to speak their minds than they'd felt before.
* _The New York Times_ [apologized for publishing an op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/f2b3256c-48c3-497b-9fc1-52ea3b62bb41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from a sitting United States Senator, which was crazy then and seems crazier in hindsight. It ultimately led to [opinion editor James Bennet's resignation](https://substack.com/redirect/7703d6aa-d886-48ff-80ff-aa875df2506b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the persistent accusation--[not without reason](https://substack.com/redirect/9aae842e-77fc-44a8-8c57-fad22fbab5d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--that the _NYT_ had become too activist.
* Fair or not, [Democrats became](https://substack.com/redirect/94f3a1ab-5eef-4f00-9acd-0517e0ae1ee5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[and are still labelled](https://substack.com/redirect/e1826d5f-6714-4263-8873-1a77d2d4e079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--as the party of the "woke" and all that entails, something [Democrats began addressing way too late](https://substack.com/redirect/a46c55b8-d270-4c5b-9343-2000f664f471?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Universities, which should be the home of open debate and discourse, [were often hostile to speakers, students, and professors from the political right](https://substack.com/redirect/7549d495-d0f4-40a1-9c2a-37ca06a5c3d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* For a while, there was a real sense that saying the wrong thing (at work, on social media, etc.) [could cost you your job](https://substack.com/redirect/d261ead7-54ef-49ca-b0ee-00fd468096ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Does that last point sound familiar? We're seeing something very similar happen [now after Charlie Kirk's assassination](https://substack.com/redirect/264225cd-4799-4591-be02-b4c77470b6ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[with the explicit encouragement of the Vice President](https://substack.com/redirect/6808574e-5d76-4c4e-9cf3-34123db98e49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I'll note.11
There was also a sense, a few years ago, that Big Tech was in the pocket of the left. [Just looking at who went to Trump's inauguration](https://substack.com/redirect/6d468cbd-c0ef-4985-b8a8-18e6fb0dd582?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [looking at who kisses the ring today](https://substack.com/redirect/a7abfb04-b404-4160-a6ff-e8c1f2b8f176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it's impossible to make that argument anymore.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=174180143&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTc0MTgwMTQzLCJpYXQiOjE3NTg3MTc3NjYsImV4cCI6MTc2MTMwOTc2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.mn6E5Q1NXVlKvH7ff5IIZir_IbgUXoYkdXq3ra-CCZ0)
### Here's the opportunity for Democrats
This is where I see an opening:
* The perceived crackdown on language and open discourse, especially once it accelerated in 2020, was unpopular and led to pushback from voters. Here's a chance to reshape the narrative.
* Tech companies, which [Republicans have seen as stifling free speech](https://substack.com/redirect/b9bd0656-e8b2-4eba-9248-3f28637f35c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),12 are squarely in the pocket of the President now. [Big Tech is also unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/62882b75-0b98-4c9b-a6b3-0e7fcc0ffa50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [trusted by few people](https://substack.com/redirect/897e2b98-1399-435f-bf14-56203ebb0beb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); Democrats can and should flip that narrative too.
* People worry their free speech is under attack--with good reason. The President and his administration are _very_ explicitly using government power to attack our right to free speech.

**Democrats should lean in hard on this issue.** Go after Republicans who have rolled over (and call out their hypocrisy). Go on Republican talk shows and podcasts.13 Don't worry about placating the annoying Democrats of Twitter, [who don't represent the average Democrat](https://substack.com/redirect/69d8af6a-5cfb-4c27-97b1-893166794514?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), much less the average voter.
There's a chance to make inroads here with voters of all stripes, especially Republicans and young men. **But that requires showing that Democrats can put their money where their mouth is, and have uncomfortable conversations in unfamiliar spaces**. Standing up for free speech is only hard when you're talking to people whose views you find objectionable.
Address the dangers of Big Tech and the perils of FCC overreach on Fox News and conservative talk radio; talk to Ben Shapiro and Megyn Kelly about policy proposals to depoliticize the FCC (to protect against the excesses of _either_ party).14 This is an issue where calling out Republican hypocrisy would bolster the argument that Democrats are making--especially if Democrats can honestly acknowledge their own issues in the past.
I hope our elected officials and candidates are up to that challenge.

1
Between [attacks on free speech](https://substack.com/redirect/1663c273-e665-4554-b3f6-fd6e680c3c2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [on the Fed](https://substack.com/redirect/aed08638-b07d-40a4-9038-710652533f44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and on [H1B visa holders](https://substack.com/redirect/a645ce09-ee93-4e21-b698-eb55f4188e8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to say nothing of a [looming government shutdown](https://substack.com/redirect/9d85524f-a1a3-4915-a943-2c25763dc65f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), there was way too much happening.
2
After all, Trump [isn't particularly popular](https://substack.com/redirect/99418df0-dcd0-4a12-8202-3046e5442a97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Moreover, when you look at how he's handling different issues (immigration, inflation, etc.), [voters generally don't think he's doing a good job](https://substack.com/redirect/7c1913be-5d0e-48df-bdc9-a212f508fe82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
3
[Bob Iger](https://substack.com/redirect/29f003a0-c1c9-4908-86b2-be41951473cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the CEO of Disney, used Disney's muted response to Florida's so-called "[Don't Say Gay](https://substack.com/redirect/cd5da4df-92d7-4e29-8001-04c957195299?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" laws a few years ago [to knife then-CEO Bob Chapek and claw his way back to power](https://substack.com/redirect/f4293d2b-634b-4c26-b6ef-293117fa2cb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The story is an interesting one, but in its shortest version: Bob Iger was the CEO of Disney and picked Bob Chapek to be his successor; after Iger left, he immediately regretted it; the two fought extensively, publicly and privately; Iger eventually got Chapek ousted and came back as CEO.
So there's a fun irony to Iger finding himself in the position of [having a former Disney CEO publicly criticize his approach](https://substack.com/redirect/389b1bdc-8f8a-46a8-bb33-d571a8eb23ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to delicate political issues.
4
My research into this was inspired by a conversation I had a couple of weeks ago, when I was hanging out with a friend of mine and his 23-year-old younger brother (who I'll call "Grant").
We ended up talking about politics, and not knowing anything about how Grant votes, I asked him a more general question: what's the political issue that you care most about?
Grant's answer: he felt like people weren't able to have a civil conversation anymore. He and his friends were worried that anything they said would ostracize friends, or get them cancelled. (Even if he recognized that "cancellation" is a pretty amorphous concept.) He's never lived in a pre-social media world and has the sense, right or wrong, that people used to more freely debate and more civilly disagree in the past.
Data is not the plural of anecdote, but Grant clearly isn't alone here.
5
The two things are correlated these days--i.e., men are more likely to be Republicans--so it's a little hard to disentangle that in the polling. Nonetheless, it's an interesting trend.
6
Very much related to all of this (and related to the footnote above, about how much Republican-leaning demographics care about free speech), here's additional data on people ages 18-34:
* Free speech is a more important issue for people who didn't go to college than people who did.
* It's a more important issue for white people than non-white people.
* It's a more important issue for men than women.

([Here's the source](https://substack.com/redirect/4b2cf308-1393-4766-a814-726a535c1248?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for all of this data.)
7
Polling done at this exact moment might find a different answer--I suspect this fear has spiked among Democrats. But this is the best data that we have to work off of.
8
My perspective: this move young men are making towards Republicans _may_ be a long-term trend, but it isn't necessarily so. If we want to change that, it's incumbent upon Democrats to reach out to young men and share a resonant message with them.
Defending free speech is part of that outreach, I think. But the problem is certainly much larger than just one policy issue.
9
A few other notes here:
* If you've ever wondered, "does Ted Cruz do a good impression of a _Goodfellas_ -era Italian-American mobster," the answer is a pretty emphatic no. But I (genuinely) respect that he went for it and committed to the bit.
* Cruz references Adam Carolla's partnership with Kimmel (on _[The Man Show](https://substack.com/redirect/8101cb31-ffe3-4c07-86d3-e4228dbf01f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_) as a golden era of Kimmel's comedy. Set aside any views you have of Kimmel (as a political figure or as a comedian), Carolla is the one who's become _really_ unwatchable. His [performance at the Alec Baldwin roast a few years ago](https://substack.com/redirect/bc411f3b-5f05-4313-9828-919e716b02a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was just brutal.

10
Albeit ones with vast reach and control over public discourse.
11
There's a [whole Wikipedia page](https://substack.com/redirect/7b851aa5-bf21-4be1-852a-89f7c616720f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) dedicated to this crackdown! And frighteningly, there's no shortage of content to fill the page.
12
In case there was any ambiguity here about how Republicans feel, that link comes from the America First Policy Institute.
13
It's cliched to talk about [Bernie Sanders going on Joe Rogan](https://substack.com/redirect/6fb9f171-20a8-4e88-a8e2-6b96a07462ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but in the sense that people watch, it works! (In any event, I think it's overly simplistic to say that Joe Rogan is cleanly part of the right-wing media.)
14
This is [clearly part of Pete Buttigieg's strategy](https://substack.com/redirect/14337dfa-1b1a-4eb8-8cd1-4f192a65da6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), looking ahead to 2028, and I think it's a good one.
